extracted.intended_audience: faculty, staff, and development officers at two-year/community colleges preparing grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for planning, locating funding, organizing, writing, and submitting grant proposals from two-year (community) colleges to government agencies, private foundations, and local industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify institution's need and develop a practical idea
rubrics_metrics.description: First, identify the institution's need and develop an idea of how the need can be met. The idea should be practical and of real importance in strengthening education at the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use relevant institutional information to demonstrate need; ensure the idea is practical and addresses an important institutional/societal problem rather than a peripheral interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build internal support and involve implementers early
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the idea with the individuals who will be involved in implementing the project. If sufficient interest is expressed and support seems forthcoming from the administration and faculty, locate a source of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Talk to potential project staff, administrators, and faculty to gauge interest and commitment before investing time in a full proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match project topic to appropriate funding source
rubrics_metrics.description: Finding a possible funding source is primarily a process of identifying a foundation or agency that has a history of funding projects in the same subject area or with a similar purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully match subject area and project purpose to funder's history and priorities; recognize that many funders have limited scopes of concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult institutional and state information resources about funders
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult your college or district development officer for information about public and private funding programs; contact your state education agency as some federal programs allocate funds to states for local projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use internal development staff and state agency contacts to learn about appropriate programs and any state-administered opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine funder publications for scope and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Most sources, especially government programs, have a pamphlet or booklet that describes their areas of interest and requirements in detail. Carefully examine the scope of concern and requirements of the possible sources of funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read program descriptions, eligibility rules, allowable uses of funds, past funded activities, and application/award procedures before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send a brief project description to prospective funders
rubrics_metrics.description: Then send a brief (no more than two pages long) description of the project, including the objectives, to agencies and foundations which seem to be interested in similar projects. A program representative will be able to determine whether the project is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep initial inquiries concise (≤2 pages) and focused on objectives so program officers can quickly assess fit; use their feedback to decide whether to prepare a full proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use grant-information organizations and publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Use resources such as The Foundation Center, Grant Information System (GIS), The Grantsmanship Center, National Council on Resource Development (NCRD), Catalog of Federal Domestic Assistance, and the Chronicle of Higher Education to locate funding sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search directories, indexes, computer-searchable catalogs, workshops, and periodicals to find appropriate funders and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and circulate a timeline with deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: A timeline with deadlines for each section of the proposal should be developed to ensure that all requirements are met by the time the proposal is due. The deadlines should be circulated to everyone involved in planning the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign responsibilities and hard deadlines; circulate schedule to all contributors and track progress to avoid last-minute omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain communication with agency/foundation representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep in touch with the agency or foundation representative so that any problems or questions can be resolved as quickly as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use program officers as a resource for clarifying requirements, eligibility, and allowable costs; clarify submission procedures early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary: clarity, precision, and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: The project summary, as well as the rest of the proposal, should be written in clear, precise language without the use of obscuring jargon. An accurate and complete description of the project objectives and procedures should be given with as much detail as possible in the length specified in the proposal guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise, avoid jargon, adhere to length limits, and ensure that summary conveys purpose, objectives, and methods clearly to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative: statement of the problem
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of the topic addressed and an explanation of both the institutional and societal needs for the project should be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use institution-specific data and context to demonstrate why the problem is important and urgent for your college and community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative: review of the literature
rubrics_metrics.description: The literature review both supports the need for the project and shows evidence that the project planners have made a detailed investigation of prior attempts to meet the need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document prior work, cite relevant research and reports (ERIC database is useful), and show how your project builds on or differs from previous efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative: clear, realistic objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: An explanation of what the project will accomplish should be provided in the narrative. These objectives should be realistic and follow directly from the statement of the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State measurable, attainable objectives that logically address the identified problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative: detailed procedures and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedures to be followed in conducting the project and the reasons for choosing these procedures should be explained in detail. The population involved, the methods used, and the materials developed are a few of the factors that should be discussed in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe step-by-step methods, sample/population characteristics, materials and instruments, and rationale for methodological choices so evaluators can assess feasibility and rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative: statement of significance
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of what the project will add to existing knowledge or how the project will improve current practices is included in the narrative to emphasize the importance of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain anticipated contributions to practice, policy, or scholarship and the broader implications for other institutions or populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative: evaluation plan (formative and summative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most funding sources require some form of evaluation, usually external, to objectively determine what the project achieved and to ensure that any recommendations made as a result of the project follow from what actually took place. The evaluation should include both formative and summative components. In this section of the report, describe the evaluation process and identify the external evaluators either generally or, if possible, by name and title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plans for ongoing (formative) assessment and final (summative) evaluation, specify evaluation questions, methods, data sources, and identify qualified external evaluators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative: dissemination of findings
rubrics_metrics.description: The process of disseminating the project findings or outcomes is described with the purpose of demonstrating the project's usefulness outside the originating institution. Include a statement that a description of the project or the final project report was submitted to ERIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe targeted dissemination channels (conferences, journals, ERIC, workshops, local partners) and plans for sharing materials/products with other institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative: staff qualifications and vitae
rubrics_metrics.description: A paragraph should be included for each principal staff member detailing his or her educational background and relevant experience or expertise. The complete vitae of staff members can be included in the appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight relevant expertise, past project roles, and include CVs in appendices; demonstrate that staff have the capacity to implement the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative: schedule of activities and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequently, the funding source requires the completion of a comprehensive schedule form showing an exact deadline for the accomplishment of each part of the project. If a form is not provided, this timeline should be included in the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear timeline or Gantt-like schedule with milestones, responsibilities, and completion dates; ensure alignment with budget and evaluation timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget statement and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The budget should be accurate and realistic. Most funding sources have a detailed budget form with spaces for each category of expense that should be addressed. Categories that are usually included are personnel costs, including benefits; equipment costs; supply expenses; travel expenses; consultant fees; other expenses; and indirect costs, such as overhead. The budget justification should support the budget figures and explain fully how the estimates were made in each category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use funder budget forms when provided; itemize categories, justify each cost, check institutional overhead/indirect cost rates, and ensure budget credibility to add authority to the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices: supporting materials and brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: The appendices should contain any additional supporting material, such as the vitae of key personnel, background material on the institution, and letters of recommendation from community members or involved individuals. Be careful not to double the size of proposals with supporting material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include only essential supporting documents; avoid unnecessary duplication of content from the main narrative; follow page/size limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal review for consistency and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: After the proposal is completed, an individual who has been closely involved in the planning process should read over the entire proposal carefully checking for consistency and continuity throughout the sections. The reader should also confirm that all the funding agency's and the college's requirements have been met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have someone (and the development office if available) perform a final compliance and continuity check to ensure all instructions, forms, and institutional approvals are included before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use evaluator feedback and consider revision if not funded
rubrics_metrics.description: Many agencies and foundations will release a copy of the evaluators’ comments to the submitters of unsuccessful proposals. These comments can provide valuable feedback and suggestions for improvement. Find out from a representative of the funding source whether the proposal can be revised and resubmitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request and review reviewer comments, revise proposals accordingly, and plan to resubmit in the next funding cycle when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present idea effectively; thoroughness and care matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The thoroughness and care that went into the proposal can make it stand out from the hundreds that the evaluators receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write clearly, be complete and careful in presentation, adhere to guidelines and timetables, and ensure the proposal demonstrates credibility and feasibility to reviewers.
